title: Account Executive (NYC)

- Native-level proficiency in English

- University degree

 

NICE TO HAVE

- SaaS, financial, fintech, or information security industries background

- Fluency in an additional language

•
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or related field;

OR demonstrable equivalent experience.

• At least 2 years of work experience in software engineering.

• Strong problem-solving skills, excellent communication and collaboration skills.

• Passionate about keeping up with modern technologies and design.

• Experience building and consuming REST APIs

Technology Must-Haves:

• C#, Python (if applicable)

• Understanding of applied OOP, SOLID, and design principles

• Strong aptitude for integrating AI/ML-driven development workflows into the daily Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC)

Technology Nice-To-Have or Dedicate to Learning Quickly:

title: Engineering Manager, Experiment Platform, Robot Software
description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Engineering Teams

Robot Software builds the on-vehicle software platform that Wayve’s AI Driver runs on. Within it, the Experiment Platform team owns the systems that let our researchers develop driving models on the road: deploying models to vehicles, running experiments, and collecting the data that trains the next model.

The team builds a portable development platform that connects to partner vehicles and brings Wayve’s model development capabilities to them, including data collection, experiment control, telemetry and over-the-air updates. It is used across our own fleet and on pre-production vehicles with OEM partners in Europe and Japan, and is central to how Wayve adapts its AI Driver to new vehicles. You will lead a team of engineers based in London, working alongside the Runtime Platform, OS, Sensors and Platform Integration teams in Robot Software.

🧠 Your day-to-day

You will lead the team’s people, plans and partnerships. Most of your time goes to your engineers: regular 1:1s, clear expectations, feedback, performance and promotion cycles, and helping technical leads take on more scope. You will work with your tech leads on technical decisions, own the outcomes, and make sure the team responds well when issues come up in the field. You will maintain the team’s mission, charter and twelve-month roadmap, turn them into quarterly and six-week plans, and keep delivery on track.

You will be the team’s main point of contact for partner engineering teams, programme managers, operations and OEM customers, and you will make it clear what the team owns.

You will stay technically capable and aware of the team’s work across the codebase. You will monitor the architecture, guide the team through technical blockers when needed, and engage with technical leaders in other teams at a technical level.

🧩 What you’ll be working on:

Growing the platform: Take the development platform from its first stable release to a product used across many vehicle types, with predictable releases and validation in CI and on HIL benches.

Experiment control and fleet orchestration: Own model and controller download, the robot state machine, and over-the-air deployment of software, configuration and calibration.

Self-serve experimentation: Make the platform self-serve, so research teams can run their own experiments on vehicles without waiting for platform changes.

Scaling data collection: Onboard and event-based logging, data quality, and data offload over

New vehicles and OEM integrations: Deploy the full platform on Wayve’s next-generation vehicles, and support new OEM integrations through configuration rather than new releases.

Building the operating model around the platform: Releases, support rota, on-call, metrics and observability.

Building the team: Own hiring and onboarding, and grow the team as adoption of the platform expands.

🙌 You should apply if:

You have managed software engineering teams, including hiring, coaching and performance management.

You have owned a platform or product that other teams or customers relied on, and shipped it to devices in the field.

You are technically capable, with hands-on experience in embedded Linux systems software (C++ or Python), and stay close enough to the code to review your team’s work, guide architecture and help resolve technical blockers.

You understand connected device fleets, such as vehicles, robots or IoT, including data logging and offload, over-the-air updates and observability.

You are comfortable leading delivery across many stakeholders, including external partners, and can engage with other technical leaders as a technical peer.

description:
This is a remote position.
Remote (US-based) · Independent contractor · ~15-20 hrs/week ongoing · Reports to the Senior Medical Director
About Shapely

Shapely is transforming the weight loss industry through an innovative physician-led approach that makes weight loss care affordable for everyone. With evidence-based care, industry-leading support, and a seamless integrated app, we help thousands of patients across California, Florida, New York, and Texas access GLP-1 therapies and comprehensive weight management, all covered by insurance, including Medicare. Most of our patients are over 65.
Our care model is longitudinal and includes MDs/DOs, NPs, PAs, and RDNs. We bill fee-for-service and also participate in MIPS.
The role
You'll be the person who makes sure what we document supports what we bill, and that we're capturing everything we legitimately earn. This is a hands-on coding and auditing role reporting to the Senior Medical Director - not a policy, billing-clerk, or general compliance position.
You'll work in two modes. Prospectively, you'll help us assess which codes are safe to use for a given visit type as well as what documentation needs to be present to use teh coe compliantly. Retrospectively, you'll audit charts to confirm the documentation holds up with high accuracy, and turn opportunities for improvement into templates, workflow fixes, and education.
What you'll do
Audit

• Conduct a baseline documentation audit (10-20 charts per billing provider) across encounters, and deliver a findings report with error rates by provider and service line

• Run ongoing quarterly audits (10 charts per provider) plus focused service-line reviews.

• Perform 100% pre-bill review during new-code rollouts until the error rate is under 5%

• Place any provider above a 10% error rate on monthly review with targeted education until they're back under threshold

Code evaluation

• Evaluate appropriateness of unused or underused codes for our care model and define the documentation each requires before we bill it

• Write documentation guidance for our clinical staff and billing team.

MIPS

• Assist with success with MIPS, including determining appropriate measures and ensuring our documentation exceeds requirements.

• Provide suggestions on enhancing our templates to optimize accuracy and compliance with MIPS

Requirements
Required

• CPC (AAPC) or CCS-P (AHIMA)

• CPMA strongly preferred, or equivalent demonstrated chart-audit experience

• 5+ years coding outpatient E/M, with direct auditing experience

• Strong knowledge of Medicare telehealth rules

• Experience with MIPS reporting and quality-measure documentation

• US-based, with strong Medicare experience

Nice to have

• Obesity medicine, endocrinology, or primary care background

• Prior work with OIG self-disclosure or payer audit response

• Experience building documentation templates or clinician cheat-sheets

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact

This isn't a relationship management role. It's an ownership role. Sharp. Adaptable. Unstoppable.

You won't wait to be asked. You'll identify what's broken before it becomes a problem, build solutions that didn't exist yesterday, and earn the kind of trust that makes you indispensable to the agency - and to Axon.

In this embedded role, you are the primary owner of customer outcomes within a strategic account - accountable for the full lifecycle of Axon's ecosystem. You combine deep technical expertise, builder instinct, operational leadership, and executive presence to help agencies transform how they operate, not just adopt software. You embed for the long haul: opening the laptop onsite, shipping on Axon's stack, holding the room when it matters, and iterating on what you build until it sticks in production.

Success is measured by the agency's operational outcomes and working solutions in production - not product health, not activity, not slideware.

What You'll Do

This role is intentionally undefined in the day-to-day. Priorities shift with agency mission tempo, operational crises, and emerging opportunities. If you need a fixed playbook to succeed, this isn't the role for you.

Building is the job. You will use Axon's platform - AI Era, agents, workflows, integrations, and data tools - to design, build, and ship new capabilities on site. You own outcomes end to end across deployment, adoption, optimization, and ongoing success - as the accountable owner, not a coordinator of other teams' work.

• Discover agency problems onsite and translate them into buildable, compliant solutions tied to mission outcomes

• Build with Axon products, not around them - configure, integrate, and extend DEMS, Fusus, AI Era, Records, and related systems in the agency environment

• Iterate in the field until adoption sticks, then document patterns for reuse across accounts

• Apply responsible innovation guardrails - CJIS, evidence integrity, privacy - in every build. Ship working software, not slideware

• Troubleshoot onsite and coordinate root-cause resolution across Product, Engineering, Support, and Services when builds or integrations break

AI Build & Adoption

• Build and deploy AI-powered workflows (agents, prompts, RAG, evaluations) that solve defined agency problems - not generic experimentation

• Drive hands-on adoption with the people who use what you build daily

• Measure whether changes stick - usage, workflow impact, mission outcomes - and iterate when they don't

Operational Transformation & Leadership

• Assess workflows onsite, identify friction and mission impact, and define what to build before you build it

• Move from reactive support to proactive outcome design - arrive with hypotheses, validate with command staff and operators, then build to match

• Build trusted relationships with agency leadership and operational stakeholders; lead QBRs, mission reviews, and strategic planning

• Define success metrics and capture baselines before major deployments so impact is proven, not assumed

title: Co-Op, Materials Science, Heterogeneous Catalysis
description:
Your Impact at LILA

As a Co-Op in Materials Science, Heterogeneous Catalysis, you will join Lila's Materials Science team at our Alewife site to help build and run high-throughput workflows for catalyst synthesis, characterization, and performance testing.

You will work hands-on in the lab: preparing catalyst samples, running reactor tests, and analyzing the resulting data for trends in structure, composition, and catalytic performance. You will work alongside scientists, automation engineers, and data scientists, and you will see how experimental work connects to AI-guided materials discovery.

This is a practical, lab-based co-op suited to a graduate student who wants real ownership of experiments and exposure to automated, data-rich science.

What You'll Be Building

• Synthesize heterogeneous catalysts and prepare samples for performance testing

• Run batch and flow reactor tests, measuring activity, selectivity, and stability

• Characterize materials using techniques such as XRD, BET, TGA, or chemisorption

• Analyze experimental data to identify structure and composition trends

• Support automated and high-throughput synthesis workflows with the engineering team

• Document protocols and results, and present findings to the team

What You'll Need to Succeed

• Currently enrolled in a Masters or PhD program in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related field

• Hands-on laboratory experience with materials synthesis or catalyst testing

• Working knowledge of common characterization techniques (XRD, BET, TGA, FTIR, or similar)

• Ability to handle chemicals safely and follow lab safety protocols

• Strong attention to detail in experimental execution and record keeping

• Clear written and verbal communication of experimental results

Bonus Points For

• Experience with batch or flow reactors, or gas sorption measurements

• Exposure to high-throughput experimentation or lab automation platforms

• Data analysis or scripting in Python, R, or MATLAB

• Coursework or research involving zeolites, MOFs, or other porous materials

About LILA

Lila Sciences is building Scientific Superintelligence™ to solve humankind's greatest challenges. We believe science is the most inspiring frontier for AI. Rather than hard-coding expert knowledge into tools, LILA builds systems that can learn for themselves.

LILA combines advanced AI models with proprietary AI Science Factory™ instruments into an operating system for science that executes the entire scientific method autonomously, accelerating discovery at unprecedented speed, scale, and impact across medicine, materials, and energy. Learn more at www.lila.ai.

Guided by our core values of truth, trust, curiosity, grit, and velocity, we move with startup speed while tackling problems of historic importance. If this sounds like an environment you'd love to work in, even if you don't meet every qualification listed above, we encourage you to apply.

Splunk Architecture & Implementation

• Cisco Meraki, Cisco Secure Network Analytics, Cisco XDR.

• Maintain accurate project documentation: HLD/LLD design artifacts, runbooks, architecture diagrams, and post-implementation reports.

Technical requirements:
Splunk Platform Expertise

• 5+ years of hands-on Splunk implementation experience in enterprise environments, including distributed multi-site deployments.

• Proven ability to architect and deploy distributed Splunk infrastructures: Indexer Clusters, Search Head Clusters, Heavy Forwarder pools, Deployment Server hierarchies, and Machine Data Lake tiers.

• Deep familiarity with Splunk Enterprise Security (ES): correlation searches, threat intelligence management, adaptive response, Risk-Based Alerting (RBA), and risk scoring frameworks.

• Working knowledge of Cisco Data Fabric architecture: federated search capabilities, data-in-place analytics, and the evolution from full-ingestion to hybrid/federated SIEM pipeline patterns.

• Familiarity with Splunk AI Toolkit, AI-assisted investigation workflows, and SOAR playbook development using Splunk SOAR is strongly advantageous.

Cisco & Network Security

• Hands-on experience integrating Cisco security products with Splunk: Secure Firewall (ASA/FTD), Secure IDS/IPS, ISE, Secure Endpoint, Umbrella, ThousandEyes, and Secure Network Analytics.

• Strong understanding of Cisco security event logging formats (syslog, eStreamer, REST/API telemetry) and their normalization into Splunk CIM data models.

• Purchasing and procurement leadership experience, including vendor management, AVL governance, and sourcing strategy; experience building or scaling category management capability is a plus.

• Experience managing long lead-time, high component-risk supply chains.

• Experience operating at scale.

• Experience leading distributed, multi-site teams, including manager-level direct reports.

Trase is the operating system for high-stakes environments, providing end-to-end solutions for deploying, managing, and optimizing AI within industries where security, governance, and data sovereignty are non-negotiable.

Our HIPAA- and SOC 2-compliant platform bridges the “last mile” of AI adoption, empowering sectors like healthcare and national security to run trustworthy, predictable AI agents across any model or environment-whether in the cloud, on-prem, or at the edge-with unified policy enforcement, continuous monitoring, and fully immutable audit trails.

Trase’s suite of products includes Origin, its agentic operating system; Leagues, its marketplace for specialized, configurable, ready-to-deploy agents; and Arena, where developers build, evaluate, and package the agents that run on Origin. The company has repeatedly topped Hugging Face’s GAIA Leaderboard for Generalized AI Assistants, placing it firmly at the forefront of AI-agent innovation.

About the Role
As a Forward Deployed Engineer at Trase, you’ll build and deploy AI agents and applications that solve real customer problems using Trase OS. You’ll join Leagues, our industry verticals team, supporting customers in healthcare, state and local government and education (SLED), financial services, or retail. Your focus may be one or more of these verticals; experience in all four is not required.
This is a hands-on software engineering role with direct customer ownership. You’ll work with users to understand their workflows, turn unclear requirements into technical plans, and take solutions from prototype through production. This role exists to:

• Deliver working solutions that improve customer workflows and produce measurable outcomes.

• Bridge customer needs and platform engineering, identifying gaps early and shaping practical solutions.

• Turn successful deployments into reusable integrations and patterns that help future customers launch faster.

What makes this role challenging

• Customer environments vary in data quality, integration options, security requirements, and operational readiness.

• AI behavior must be evaluated against real workflows, including failure cases, escalation paths, and human review.

• You must balance delivery speed with reliability and maintainability, while deciding what belongs in a customer solution versus the shared platform.

Responsibilities

• Work directly with customers to map workflows, identify useful AI applications, and agree on scope, success measures, and acceptance criteria.

• Build production-quality agents, applications, APIs, and integrations using Trase OS, including backend services and user interfaces as needed.

• Integrate customer systems, data sources, and identity providers; work with infrastructure engineers to deploy in customer or Trase-managed environments.

• Own delivery through testing, deployment, customer validation, and operational handoff. Surface dependencies, risks, and scope changes early.

• Build evaluations, automated tests, observability, and human review or escalation into agent workflows; validate quality, latency, cost, and reliability.

• Apply appropriate access controls, data-handling policies, and audit logging in partnership with Security and customer teams.

ABOUT SUPABASE

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Builders now ask ChatGPT & Claude before they ask Google, and the answer decides which products make the shortlist. When someone asks about a backend as a service or a database, Supabase should be in that answer: named, cited, and recommended. You’ll own that channel and will be responsible with driving signups and revenue. You set the strategy and execute the work with content, growth product, and engineering.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

- Own the GEO/AEO strategy: decide which prompts matter, set targets, and sequence the roadmap

- Build measurement for a channel with messy attribution

- Run experiments to learn what actually moves citations, then turn the results into a playbook

- Work with the content team to decide the human and LLM content roadmap.

- Win citations from the ones used the most in pre training: Reddit, YouTube, review sites, listicles, publications, and communities

- Make the site readable for agents. Ship these changes with web and engineering

- Track where competitors get named and we don’t, and close those gaps

- Keep SEO fundamentals compounding, since they still feed AI retrieval

- Teach the rest of the company how to write and structure content so it gets cited, and share what you learn with PMM, product, and leadership

- Stay ahead of the market

YOU MIGHT BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU

- 4+ years in SEO, organic growth, or content-led acquisition at a developer tool

- 1+ year of hands-on GEO/AEO work.

- A track record you can show: citations you won, AI referral traffic you grew, share of voice you moved, and how you measured it and connected it to revenue

- Technically fluent: crawling, indexing, structured data, site architecture, and log analysis. Comfortable getting changes shipped with engineers

WHAT WE OFFER

- Fully Remote

We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

- ESOP

Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

- Tech Allowance

Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment-laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

- Health Benefits

Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

- Annual Off-Sites

Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

- Flexible Work

We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

- Professional Development

Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning-courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

- ~400 team members

- 60+ countries

- 20+ languages spoken

- Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

- 540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support-not replace-existing tools and communities.

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year - far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

Ramp builds software that moves real money, from bill payments and corporate cards to reimbursements, accounting integrations, and travel. Our customers rely on us to keep their operations running: invoices get paid, books get closed, and finance leaders can trust the data behind every decision.

This is not script-based support. You will triage, investigate, and make high-signal judgment calls throughout the day.

Additionally, by creating value-based contracts across a wide variety of health plans, we aim to flip the script on the traditional fee-for-service model. If you want to help create a health care system that is good for patients, good for practices and good for society - and if you're eager to join a collaborative, inclusive and remote-first culture - you've come to the right place.
 
What Does This Mean for You?
At Aledade PBC, you will be part of a creative culture that is driven by a passion for tackling complex issues with respect, open-mindedness and a desire to learn.
